findings.summary: The selected Free-plan manual backup posture does not satisfy the literal managed-database-backup contract.
findings.evidence: Brief AC-14 and design OPS-005 require selected cloud-provider managed backup defaults. Supabase reports no owner-accessible daily database backup or PITR for the Free project. Stages 5 and 11 instead prove an authenticated-encrypted logical dump uploaded to a private bucket in the separate Sydney Steady backups project and restored successfully. This is a credible low-cost control, but the repository correctly states that it is not a managed database backup. Review cannot silently reinterpret AC-14. Return to Define to amend the contract to the owner-selected manual-backup control, or select a plan that provides managed backups.

findings.summary: The retained public Heroku rollback service still exposes the retired privileged machine-route surface.
findings.evidence: On 2026-08-24 unauthenticated production checks returned 401, not 404, for /api/chat/capabilities and /api/agent/feelings, confirming that the public rollback service still registers both token-protected routes. Heroku also retains CHAT_INGEST_TOKEN and AGENT_API_TOKEN config names. The agent route accepts a caller-selected user identity after shared-token authentication, which is intentionally absent from the replacement. Keeping Go/Heroku recoverable does not require keeping these retired privileged endpoints publicly usable throughout observation. Before cutover, Define/Design/Plan must specify an explicitly authorized control that disables their secrets/routes or isolates rollback ingress while preserving browser-route rollback.

findings.summary: The retained MongoDB application credential has broader privileges than the rollback source requires.
findings.evidence: Stage 5 records that the production Go/Heroku Mongo credential still has atlasAdmin@admin access. The application and rollback tooling require only scoped access to the feeling database and collections. Because Heroku/Mongo must remain recoverable through observation, this broad credential remains live during the highest-risk migration window. Before production cutover, provision and verify least-privilege browser-service and rollback access, or obtain an explicit named waiver after documenting the exact Atlas role and blast radius. Any Atlas or Heroku credential change requires separate production authority.

findings.summary: The shipped legacy React client has direct and transitive dependency advisories tracked outside this migration.
findings.evidence: The current audit reports 82 findings: 15 low, 17 moderate, 42 high, and 8 critical. Direct affected packages are axios, moment, postcss, and react-scripts. The API uses fixed same-origin endpoints and strict server-side validation, while postcss/react-scripts are build tooling, so npm severity is not accepted as application exploitability without analysis. On 2026-08-24 Vinicius Delascio directed remediation to separately Defined FOLLOWUP-REACT-001. The findings remain visible and unwaived; that follow-up must perform reachability analysis and modernization.

findings.summary: Azure Review evidence was refreshed with modern authentication while Security Defaults remained enabled.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Security Defaults correctly rejected device-code flow for the new tenant. Vinicius Delascio completed browser-based modern authentication against tenant 8e263016-4fa0-4d3c-a7f2-7cc76d872ccb and the isolated personal subscription. Read-only checks verified Australia East, healthy r2/r3 revisions on the approved digest, r3 at 100 percent, scale 0..1, only database-url as a secret reference, ACR admin disabled, managed-identity AcrPull only, 30-day Log Analytics retention, monthly 5 budget/80-percent alert, 17 counted requests and zero restarts over seven days. The unrelated corporate subscription was not used.

findings.summary: Current history size does not require a pagination contract change, but scale-to-zero latency remains observable.
findings.evidence: The largest hosted history is 106 records and approximately 50,464 JSON bytes, below the documented 500-row/250-KiB review guardrail. Azure's first request after scale-to-zero took approximately 26 seconds; warm readiness and unauthorized API checks were approximately 0.09 seconds. The monitoring runbook records both the growth trigger and cold-start trade-off. Changing minimum replicas remains a separately approved cost/infrastructure decision.

acceptance_criteria_evidence.evidence: Stages 7, 8 and 11: exact feelings contract, hosted RLS integration, source/target differential verification, full 114-row reconciliation and authenticated browser read.
Stages 7, 8 and 11: strict POST contract, one-write persistence, verified-sub ownership, subsequent read, two-subject isolation and hosted rollback-only tests.
Stages 9 and 11: weekly empty-result envelope record:null through service, HTTP, integration, differential and browser verification.
Stages 4, 9 and 11: unique user/week schema, atomic ON CONFLICT upsert, concurrency test, version/timestamp mapping and full browser journey.
Stages 6, 7, 9 and 11: RS256 issuer/audience/expiry/sub validation, missing/invalid/mismatched credential matrix, no-write assertions and cross-user RLS denial.

Owner confirmed OpenClaw no longer exists; Stages 1, 10 and 13 found no current caller in repository/config inventory. The public rollback service still registers the routes and is separately raised as REV-002 before Release.
Stage 10 exact route/config tests prove the replacement exposes none of chat, agent or ping and requires none of their secrets or privileged identity paths.
Stages 8, 9, 11 and 12: React contract/journey suites and retained-account Azure same-origin login, reload, read, weekly navigation and logout without relinking or re-registration.
Stages 1, 7, 9, 10 and 11: approved quirk normalization, empty array, strict validation, structured statuses/errors, pre-handler CORS rejection and ping removal.

Stages 3 through 5 and 11: Sydney target/backup projects, deterministic migration of 114 feelings and 2 weekly trackers, five ownership keys, approved normalization, zero exceptions/target-only rows and successful encrypted restore rehearsal.
Stages 4, 6, 7, 9, 11 and 12: private schema, no Data API grants, non-BYPASSRLS roles, forced RLS, nine hosted policies, two-subject direct/API tests and no operator application route.
Stage 11 full nonproduction verification: 114/2 counts, keyed reconciliation, contracts, negative security matrix, browser journey and no unapproved discrepancy.
Stage 12: healthy Azure revision reversal, pre-commit procedure, disposable post-write reconciliation to Mongo, second-run idempotency and forward zero-discrepancy proof.

Owners, secret-name inventory, monitoring, support, audit, incident, cutover and rollback procedures exist and production remains unchanged. However the selected Free project has no owner-accessible managed database backup, so the manual encrypted logical-backup control does not meet the literal managed-backup clause. REV-001 requires a Define amendment or a managed-backup plan.

approval.reason: Pending resolution of the three open high-severity findings and explicit accountable Review approval. This Review does not authorize Release or any production mutation.
